sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Madhur Knit Crafts is a mixed-quality, cash-constrained textile growth watchlist, not an evidence-backed compounder. BQS is 4.94/10; GQS is 5.00 after the persistent-cash-conversion cap, versus 5.80 raw; IAS is NS. Genuine organic volume growth, integration and a larger customer base are the strengths. Negative cumulative operating cash, older receivables and inventory absorption are the decisive weaknesses. Known IPO funding is substantial and makes an automatic distress conclusion inappropriate. However, the ₹56.50 official close on 19 October does not establish an attractive funded return merely because trailing P/E is low.

This is an operating expansion and margin-recovery thesis, not a demonstrated long-duration compounder. All four gates are Conditional, not evidenced Fail. No fraud or loan default is inferred from old control weaknesses or a non-cooperating credit rating. Better evidence of post-IPO deployment, debt, collections and inventory normalization could improve the price-sensitive conclusion. A lower quote alone cannot cure the missing funding and implementation evidence. [E02,E03,E06,E07,E10–E15]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Madhur Knit Crafts Limited, formerly Madhur Knit Crafts Private Limited, was incorporated on 21 August 1997 and converted on 30 January 2025. Its CIN is U17301PB1997PLC020381. The investable security is NSE SME MADHURKNIT, ISIN INE1P5601010. The eligible SM master row verifies 19,009,232 issued shares and a 1,200-share market lot. The company has no subsidiaries in the reviewed perimeter; standalone Indian GAAP under the Companies Accounting Standards applies, not Ind AS.

The research cutoff is 20 October 2026, UTC. The market reference is the official 19 October close of ₹56.50, giving ₹107.4022 crore equity capitalization. This is not a live executable quote. The analytical holding period is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, with a 15% nominal annual equity hurdle before personal taxes. DCF WACC of 13–18% is a separate assumption. The illustrative ₹5 lakh position is not a recommended allocation: its whole-lot floor is seven lots, 8,400 shares and ₹474,600; the ceiling is eight lots, 9,600 shares and ₹542,400.

Confidence is High on identity and retrieved official prices, Medium on historical earnings, organic growth and capital attribution, and Low on current funding allocation, price-implied expectations and complete liquidity. G1 concerns minority protection, G2 reliability, G3 funding and G4 tradability. Their Conditional findings are distinct. Overall investment confidence follows the weakest material input rather than an average. [E01,E09–E15]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
BQS raw and final are 4.94, displayed as 4.9/10, with 100% factor coverage. GQS raw is 5.80 and final is 5.00 because CASH=2 reflects persistent poor realization over four profitable years, not merely an expansion-capex cycle. IAS is NS, with 45% coverage, a known weighted contribution of 2.035 and a mathematical missing-factor bound of 2.585–7.535. This is not a statistical confidence interval or a rankable midpoint.

The canonical factors are GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 7, DUR 5, CAP 6, CASH 2, BAL 5, EXEC 6, EARN 6, R NS, D 4, P NS and L NS. The preferred five-year revenue CAGR of 25.84% starts REV at 8; one negative adjustment recognizes the demonstrable pandemic-low base. No additional small-company or half-year trajectory penalty is applied. BQS enters IAS once at its exact, unrounded value. Moving GOV and CAP independently by one point changes BQS by 0.20 and 0.12; the joint interpretive range is 4.62–5.26. CAP ±1 moves raw GQS by 0.15 but leaves its cash cap at 5. No governance or funding-failure numeric override is applied. Exact Decimal weights, contributions and bounds are embedded. [E02,E06,E08,E10–E15]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The Ludhiana operation converts yarn and grey cloth through knitting, dyeing, printing, stentering, brushing or raising, and finishing. Products include polyester, spun, acrylic and cotton-blend fabrics for garments and blankets, with a small technical paint-roller application. FY2025 revenue of ₹171.635 crore was 85.21% knitted cloth, 6.45% garments, 4.27% job work, 3.43% blankets and 0.63% scrap.

This is primarily B2B supply to wholesalers and local fabric buyers, not a consumer brand with demonstrated pricing premiums. Sales were entirely domestic; Punjab contributed 94.04% in FY2025 and 98.18% in the eleven months to February 2026. Orders precede production, but that does not eliminate raw-material inventory, unsold work in process or buyer credit. The top ten suppliers comprised 54.23% of procurement in FY2025, versus 34.15% of sales for the top ten customers. Money is earned from manufactured or traded fabric and processing, then collected later. Consequently, growth depends on both conversion economics and credit-funded working capital. [E04–E07,E12]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Integration can shorten turnaround and retain more conversion value. Local relationships and product breadth create a useful operating position. Outsourced grey-cloth and job-work intensity declined from 64.16% of revenue in FY2023 to 37.53% in FY2025 as output scaled. Yet the reviewed records do not establish protected technology, durable switching costs, persistent price premiums or strong cash returns through a full cycle. More customers improve bargaining balance without proving contractual retention.

Kaytex is a nearby fabric, digital-printing and ethnic-product integration comparator. Nitin Spinners provides a larger integrated yarn, knitted/woven fabric and export-diversification benchmark. Siyaram illustrates branded distribution that Madhur has not demonstrated. These are economic comparisons, not interchangeable valuation multiples or claims that each peer is investable. No current peer-price table is fabricated. The stronger-peer lesson is that integration is not unique; the weaker interpretation of Madhur is that recent margins reflect replicable integration and utilization rather than a structural advantage. MOAT 4 recognizes that limitation without denying real process capability. [E03–E05,E17]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue was ₹66.8734, ₹77.3974, ₹89.3270, ₹108.3845, ₹171.6350 and ₹211.0345 crore in FY2021–FY2026. The preferred five-year CAGR is 25.84%; the three-year CAGR is 33.19%. FY2020 revenue of ₹86.9739 crore gives 15.92% over six years and exposes the pandemic-low starting year. Annual additions were ₹10.5239, ₹11.9296, ₹19.0575, ₹63.2505 and ₹39.3995 crore. No acquired perimeter was identified, so the expansion is organic.

Physical output rose 58.75% in FY2024 and 60.87% in FY2025, versus revenue growth of 21.33% and 58.36%. Product mix, traded inputs and outsourcing changed, so revenue divided by kilograms is a blended cross-check, not a like-for-like selling price. Knitted-cloth mix rose from 61.29% to 76.15% to 85.21%. Customer count increased from 366 to 418 to 497; new-customer revenue increased from ₹14.2249 to ₹29.2068 to ₹39.1201 crore. Retained-customer revenue of ₹75.1020, ₹79.1778 and ₹132.5149 crore is not net revenue retention, lifetime value or cohort profitability. Those customer economics are not disclosed.

FY2026 revenue growth slowed to 22.96%. H2 revenue of ₹97.2923 crore versus ₹97.8224 crore was almost flat, while PAT increased about 14.47%. H2 is a balancing figure using unaudited, unreviewed H1, not an independently audited half-year. REV 7 applies one distorted-base adjustment; this half-year does not attract a second penalty. [E02–E05]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Installed capacity increased from 2.4 million kilograms in FY2023 to 3.75 million in FY2024 and 7.5 million in FY2025. FY2025 output of 4.8382 million kilograms implies 64.51% utilization and about 2.66 million kilograms of nominal headroom. Eleven-month FY2026 output of 5.23125 million divided by annual capacity is 69.75%; it is explicitly not annualized utilization.

The base model reaches terminal trailing revenue of about ₹396.67 crore at 12% annual growth. Using the FY2025 blended revenue/output cross-check of about ₹355 per kilogram suggests more than 11 million kilograms, above installed capacity. That scale requires added capacity, different mix or realization, or more outsourced conversion. The model therefore includes annual capex of 2.5% of sales plus ₹3.675 crore for solar, and ONWC of 42.5% of sales. This is an analytical funding path, not contracted demand or an announced, fully financed textile expansion. Disclosed February capital commitments of ₹1.2213 crore net of advances fit within ordinary forecast capex; they are not deducted again.

Customer breadth and utilization headroom support DUR 5. Local demand concentration, seasonal exposure and collections constrain duration. CAP 6 uses a stable-organic multi-year capital bridge, not a claimed solar-project return. CASH 2 caps GQS at 5 despite strong real growth. Solar supplier projections remain unachieved until ordered, commissioned and measured. [E03,E05,E06,E08,E13,E18]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The prospectus shows post-issue promoter-group ownership of 70.55%. Current encumbrances were not independently reconciled, so no unqualified no-pledge claim is made. The IPO was fresh company capital with no OFS. FY2025 related purchases were ₹40.6671 crore, related sales ₹5.9005 crore and remuneration ₹0.6612 crore, about 6% of restated PAT. These transactions require economic scrutiny but are not automatically abusive. Related demand loans remain debt, not assumed permanent equity. The National Yarn Agency payable increased from ₹0.6662 crore to ₹11.3429 crore by February 2026, making supplier funding material.

CARE's 13 May 2025 B-/A4 issuer-not-cooperating rationale is a dated information warning, not a default rating. The August 2026 prospectus says no principal or interest default in the preceding three years; FY2025 CARO also reports no default. Minor statutory payment delays are disclosed, with management stating subsequent payment including interest or fees and stronger processes. This does not conflict with CARO's narrower statement of no undisputed arrears beyond six months.

Earlier missing bank-return evidence and the FY2024 ineffective audit trail are real. FY2025's active trail, no detected tampering, reconciled bank returns and unmodified IFC provide meaningful remediation, not retrospective certainty. Operating output and customer expansion were delivered; solar commissioning, savings and actual IPO debt retirement are not assumed delivered. The 18 September price-query response attributes movement to market forces and denies an undisclosed material event. Preserve that response without treating it as independent proof of price integrity. [E10–E13,E16,E18,E19]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY2026 revenue was ₹211.0345 crore, EBIT ₹24.8246 crore, EBITDA ₹27.4829 crore and PAT ₹13.0189 crore. Other income was only ₹0.1135 crore. Value added before labour, processing and other conversion costs was ₹61.6571 crore; it is not a fully defined gross profit.

FY2023–FY2026 cumulative CFO of −₹2.5959 crore divided by PAT of ₹26.6588 crore is −9.74%. Capex is not an explanation for weak CFO. Inventory absorbed ₹25.8323 crore in FY2026 while trade and other payables supported cash. Reported CFO is before financing-classified cash interest: FY2026 CFO ₹3.6871 crore becomes −₹3.8177 crore after ₹7.5048 crore cash interest, and −₹9.0435 crore after cash capex. The safe historical table preserves this distinction for every year. Original FY2025 cash interest was ₹5.8399 crore versus ₹5.9399 crore restated; neither is silently replaced by accrual interest. March unrestricted CCE was ₹0.3202 crore, versus cash and bank balances of ₹0.3848 crore. Gross debt was ₹73.2984 crore; net debt/EBITDA was 2.66× and EBIT interest cover 3.33×.

FY2025 statutory PAT of ₹10.3861 crore becomes ₹11.0325 crore restated through ₹0.2194 crore gratuity and ₹0.4270 crore deferred-tax adjustments. CFO, CFI and CFF differ by classification, but total cash movement and closing CCE reconcile within rounding. That supports bounded use of the figures; it does not retrospectively cure historical controls. FY2021 receivables use the later regrouped ₹21.0722 crore comparator, not the original ₹24.4576 crore presentation: ₹3.3855 crore moved to advances. The balance sheet also contains a ₹0.0600 crore non-operating investment. FY2024's capital-component residual is ₹0.1417 crore deferred-tax asset, not operating working capital.

Broad capital is assets less cash, trade payables and other current liabilities. FY2023–FY2026 capital increased from ₹50.3135 crore to ₹123.2144 crore; NOPAT at 25% tax increased from ₹2.8998 crore to ₹18.61845 crore. The incremental ratio is 21.56%, versus 19.66% over five years, and current average-capital ROIC is 16.64%. Small non-operating items and tax/GST balances are explicitly identified in this conservative broad proxy. FY2026's financing reconciliation residual of ₹6.0267 crore equals deferred tax ₹1.7742 crore, long provisions ₹0.2231 crore and short provisions ₹4.0294 crore.

FY2024 fixed investment of ₹13.1995 crore reconciles cash capex ₹15.4930 less increased advances ₹2.5700 plus capital creditors ₹0.2765. FY2025 gross additions of ₹13.4235 include ₹6.2742 crore transferred from CWIP, leaving ₹7.1493 crore fresh investment. Its cash/advance/creditor reconstruction is ₹7.2406 crore, leaving a bounded ₹0.0913 crore timing/classification residual. MD&A commissioned-capacity spending is a different measure from cash capex. Roughly three quarters of the EBIT increment comes from integration or margin recovery, including old assets. CAP 6 does not present the aggregate ratio as a new-project return. [E06–E10]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹56.50, market capitalization of ₹107.4022 crore implies 8.25× FY2026 PAT using current issued shares. Historical weighted EPS of ₹9.69 would misleadingly suggest 5.83×; current-share-equivalent EPS is ₹6.849. Current price combined with March debt/cash gives 6.56× EV/EBITDA, explicitly a date-mismatched historical cross-check, not current October EV.

The model starts at March 2026, dates IPO cash to 1 September, values entry on 20 October 2026 and ends cash funding on 20 October 2031. Bear/base/bull assumptions are revenue growth of 2/12/18%, EBIT margin of 7.5/11/12.5%, ONWC of 49/42.5/40% of sales, annual capex of 2.5/2.5/3.5% of sales and exit EBITDA multiples of 5/7/9×. Full annual and monthly rows reconcile cash, interest, tax, capital investment, debt and shares. The FY2032 operating projection informs terminal trailing earnings using the actual leap-year day fraction, but no post-terminal cash gap affects the investor horizon.

Total issue fees of ₹4.9265 crore are counted once. ₹0.1791 crore incurred by 11 May is conservatively assumed settled then; only ₹4.7474 crore is deducted from IPO cash. IPO uses include debt ₹20.85 crore, solar ₹3.675 crore and full GCP ₹7.9 crore. Working-capital funding is consumed through ONWC, not paid a second time. Prepayment penalties must use internal resources. March short provisions of ₹4.0294 crore are conservatively settled once; their detailed composition is not disclosed in the result. Current tax is separate. Opening deferred tax liability of ₹1.7742 crore is not interest-bearing debt; an optional full-settlement resource sensitivity is retained because reversal timing is unknown. The ₹0.2231 crore long-provision claim is deducted once. Capital creditors and advances remain within the broad cash bridge, not a second debt claim. There is no extra value for operating property, no assumed release of restricted cash, and no legal-recovery proceeds.

Ordinary IRRs and entry prices are NS. Every original non-rescue path breaches the minimal ₹0.25 crore cash floor before entry, so its conditional returns also remain NS. These hypothetical monthly gaps do not establish an actual historical default. Known IPO resources can absorb a substantial potential bridge liability, supporting G3 Conditional rather than a mechanical Hold. Exact deployment, debt and earmark timing still limit current return support. Separate whole-share rescue models use a 25% reference-price discount and 5% fees, exposing dilution without assuming financing is available.

Base 7× exit EBITDA produces an algebraic terminal price near ₹173.24 and a 15%-discounted diagnostic near ₹86.14. The 15% WACC/3% terminal-growth DCF cross-check is only about ₹53.21, with 80.35% of operating EV from terminal value. Neither is an entry target. Terminal DCF reinvestment uses 15% ROIC including required operating cash. The reverse solver finds no funded crossing and never substitutes an endpoint. Embedded sensitivities include growth/multiple, 12/15/18% equity hurdles, WACC/terminal growth, working capital, margins, capex, interest, cash reserve, prepayment penalties and execution costs. [E13–E15]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case links weaker local or winter demand with slower collections, older inventory, lower utilization and higher interest. Related supplier credit may stop expanding at exactly the wrong time. Gross receivables older than six months were 40.59% of gross receivables in February 2026, versus 28.66% in FY2025, while provisioning remained small. This is a credit-risk warning, not proof every overdue balance is lost.

Under the base assumptions, post-entry cash bottoms near ₹12 crore. A two-percentage-point margin decline nearly consumes the minimal buffer; five extra percentage points of ONWC or two extra percentage points of capex produce post-entry breaches. Bear algebraic terminal value near ₹38.28 before counterfactual rescue is roughly 32% below the reference price; rescue adds ownership dilution. These are conditional economics, not predictions or proved unpaid obligations.

Known IPO funding and the more recent no-default disclosures are the strongest evidence against immediate distress. Permanent-loss risk is nevertheless High because credit losses, adverse dilution and valuation normalization can coincide. D=4 recognizes material impairment risk without using a severe-default score. The thesis-break variable is the conversion of inventory and receivables into cash without recurring adverse financing, not reported revenue growth alone. [E06,E07,E11,E13,E14]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A multibagger outcome is not the investment premise. Over five years, 5× requires 37.97% annual price growth and 10× requires 58.49%. With unchanged margins, shares and P/E, revenue would need to increase fivefold or tenfold, far beyond installed capacity and demonstrated internal funding. Five years of 12% profit growth produces only 1.76× earnings; 18% produces 2.29×, before dilution.

A larger outcome therefore needs several additional successes: funded capacity, credit discipline, durable margins and valuation support. None follows from a small market capitalization. Enterprise value can expand while per-share wealth disappoints if new capital is repeatedly required. The 5×/10× claim is speculative and unsupported by the present evidence, though not mathematically impossible. No precise success probability or promotional price target is assigned. [E03,E06,E08,E13,E14]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
The proposed review cadence is public half-year/annual reporting and material filings, not an automatically scheduled service. Eight specific checks matter:
1. Reconcile actual IPO use against ₹48.3415 crore net, including debt ₹20.85 crore and solar ₹3.675 crore, before crediting deleveraging or savings.
2. Improve cumulative cash conversion from −9.74%. Another year of CFO below PAT is an alert; worsening aged balances with unexplained funding is a potential thesis break.
3. Track inventory from ₹64.7722 crore in March 2026. Inventory/sales remaining above 30.7% while growth slows is a warning, compared with FY2025's 22.7%.
4. Verify collection and provisioning for February receivables older than six months of ₹20.1820 crore out of ₹49.7161 crore gross. Further ageing requires credit analysis, not a generic growth explanation.
5. Rerun funding jointly if EBIT margin falls below 9% and ONWC rises, versus FY2026 EBIT margin of 11.76%.
6. Confirm commissioned capacity and customer access before forecasting output above the 7.5 million kilogram installed base.
7. Inspect full FY2026 CARO, audit-trail and IFC reporting and any new CARE cooperation update. A material unexplained discrepancy changes G2, not just a decimal score.
8. Build sixty verified listed sessions and resolve missing rows, spreads, circuits and practical lot capacity before a liquidity conclusion.
Solar milestones are ordered, installed, commissioned and measured savings. Top-line growth alone cannot cure cash risk. [E03,E06,E07,E10,E11,E13–E15,E18]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: insufficient evidence for a current price-sensitive investment conclusion; mixed-quality, cash-constrained growth research watchlist. BQS 4.94 and capped GQS 5.00 are historical business assessments, not purchase instructions. IAS is NS and cannot enter a numerical investment ranking. The matrix cannot be completed by inventing R, P or L.

All four gates are Conditional. No fraud, actual loan default or evidenced failure is asserted. The company does not qualify as an evidence-backed compounder: MOAT 4, CASH 2 and several other factors fall below the required thresholds. Action category is Research priority: establish cash deployment and collections before investment consideration. No ordinary entry range is endorsed.

A verified post-IPO funding bridge could improve R and P without changing historical business quality. Sustained cash realization and repeat incremental returns would be needed for a quality upgrade. Personal holdings, taxes, risk budget and live execution are unknown. This document neither allocates capital nor instructs a trade. [E06,E08,E10–E15]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source register contains primary URLs, dates, original SHA256 digests and locators. Evidence types separate verified disclosures (V), calculations (C), attributed management statements (M) and analyst assumptions (A). FY2021–FY2022 use original statutory accounts, FY2023–FY2025 IPO-restated accounts and FY2026 audited results. Comparability differences remain visible. Full historical statutory audit annexures were inspected, not just opinion headings. The FY2026 full annual statutory package was not located; a recent Reg33 audit does not replace CARO and IFC.

Open questions include actual IPO deployment and earmarks, post-IPO debt and available drawing power, aged-debtor collections, inventory ageing, historical bank-return remediation, promoter encumbrances, product-level selling prices/margins and new-project returns. The prospectus discloses ₹0.0031 crore pending TDS interest and recovery claims of ₹0.1284649 crore, ₹0.20 crore and ₹0.7942498 crore, the last including ₹0.3283667 crore interest. These claims are not incoming cash or added asset value; hearing status may be stale. An income-tax matter appears as positive ₹0.0145 crore in the financial note and negative ₹0.0145 crore in MD&A. The unexplained sign is retained, not treated as a receivable release. Capital commitments of ₹1.2213 crore are covered within forecast capex, not paid twice.

Tax of 25%, WACC of 13–18%, terminal ROIC of 15%, capital intensity, exit multiples and the minimal cash floor are analyst assumptions, not guidance. Original issuer PDFs, OCR, HTML, page images and personal identifiers are excluded from the private analytical backups. Safe extracts support calculation reproduction, not fresh original-source authentication. Authentication requires retrieving the cited originals and comparing their digests. valuation.units: INR crore, shares in absolute units
limitations: No post-IPO deployment/current unrestricted cash or available drawing-power confirmation located. Models are scenarios, not proof of a real deficit or financing availability.

Actual August 2026 loan certificate and no-default statement counter an inference of historical default. Pre-entry monthly rows are diagnostic because actual seasonal cash flows and bank drawings are unavailable.

IPO cash receipt modeled on listing date 1 September, not retrospectively available from March. Total fees4.9265 include0.1791 incurred by May11; conservatively assumed settled in cash on May11, that cash charge is modeled on May11 and only remaining4.7474 deducted at IPO, so total issue fees counted once. Actual prepayment timing before May11 is unknown. Target debt prepayment and full solar/GCP spending modeled immediately, while working-capital object is retained as permitted operating funding and is consumed only through modeled ONWC.
The minimal 0.25 crore cash floor is not a comfort buffer. Sensitivity raises it to 1 crore. No unutilized bank facility is invented.

Old March short-term provisions paid once; their detailed FY26 composition is ND and treating the full amount as payable is conservative. Current cash tax is modeled separately. Noncash DTA is not spendable. Opening DTL1.7742 is not ordinary interest-bearing debt; no specific reversal date is disclosed. A separate resource-envelope sensitivity assumes full cash settlement rather than silently releasing it. Long gratuity claim deducted once in equity bridge; no separate operating-property value. Capital-creditor/advance timing is within broad ONWC; no second debt deduction.

Related-party demand loans remain included in debt and are not assumed forgiven. Scheduled pre-IPO maturities and target IPO prepayments do not double-count the same FY27 debt; subsequent 2 crore annual maturity is an assumption tested through stresses.
No dividend or additional warrants. Rescue is explicitly counterfactual, at 25% discount to reference price with 5% fees; pre-entry rescue is not represented as an actual historical event.
Monthly uniform accrual ignores winter seasonality, so monthly solvency is only a sensitivity. Full FY32 operating projection informs terminal TTM, but funding stops 20 October 2031, not March 2032.

G3 can be Conditional rather than mechanically Hold; returns remain NS.
